Places were dropped; Thorn was disqualified; Elson when favourably placed had to give up owing to leg weariness, and as the race progressed our position became worse and worse, finally ending as the result shows below.
However, Len Fletcher again followed Hyde home, and led our team to their third scratch team win. Frank Thorn showed a return to form in finishing fifth and was our second man home.

Meanwhile Green had made third position secure, and with Elson seventh, and Thorn tenth, we again proved easy scratch team winners. In addition, this team were placed second in the team handicap and our "C" team were third.
Thorn kept Len company for a while, but then experienced leg trouble which caused him to stop for a few minutes and lose several places which could not afterwards be regained.

Thorn was fancied to win and right from the start it was evident that he was determined to do so as convincingly as possible. Taking the lead immediately he opened a gap of 120 yards in the first mile and this advantage he increased steadily and evenly throughout to win eventually by about 600 yards.
Fletcher, the County champion, and Thorn, both suffered disqualification and this put paid to our hopes of winning the championship for the first time.
Thorn was second and in his walking he gave the impression that he was out to walk in good style rather than attempt to beat Fletcher, or put up a fast time.

Thorn, the holder, had a chill and did not start. This robbed the fight for the trophy of a good deal of interest, as although Harry Churcher had been walking brilliantly during the past few months and had beaten Thorn, he had not shewn time quite equal to the latter's in last year's race.
